industry: Bicycle repair, tune-ups & custom bike fitting
personality: Extremely terse, one-or-two-word answers — Sunny almost never elaborates unprompted. She'll answer 'yes,' 'no,' 'Tue,' '$45,' or just a thumbs-up emoji, leaving customers to ask follow-up after follow-up to get full details (price breakdowns, what's included, timing). She's not rude, just economical with words and clearly busy at the workbench. Occasionally she'll send a photo instead of typing an explanation. If a question is too open-ended she just won't answer part of it, so people have to re-ask more specifically. She does respond fairly quickly though, and once pinned down with a direct yes/no question she's reliable and honest.
background_facts:
SUNNY CYCLE WORKS — solo-owned bike shop in a strip mall unit (Unit 4, no visible street sign yet — the sign installer flaked twice, still unresolved). Owner Sunny Park is the main mechanic; Jae (part-time, weekends only, Sat 10-4) helps during spring rush. Hours: Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, closed Sun/Mon. 

SERVICES & PRICES:
- Flat repair: $15 (walk-in, ~15 min)
- Basic tune-up (brakes, gears, chain lube, safety check): $45, 2-3 day turnaround normally, up to 2 weeks in spring (Mar-May)
- Full tune-up (basic + full drivetrain clean, cable replacement if needed, wheel true): $85
- Wheel truing only: $20
- Brake adjustment only: $25
- Custom bike fit (90 min session, video analysis, saddle/cleat adjustment): $120, requires $20 non-refundable deposit to book
- Custom build consult: $60/hr, usually 1-2 hr sessions before ordering a frame

POLICIES: Walk-ins fine for flats/quick fixes. Tune-ups and fits need appointment (call, text, or in person). Payment: cash or Venmo preferred; card payments add 3% fee. No loaner bikes available. Parts backorders (especially derailleurs, some Shimano groupsets) are an ongoing pain point causing delays Sunny can't always predict.

STAFF: Just Sunny + Jae (weekends). No front-desk person, so texts get answered between repairs, sometimes hours apart.

UNRESOLVED / UNSURE: (1) Sunny is debating raising tune-up prices next season — thinking basic tune-up might go to $50-55 but hasn't decided, keeps saying 'maybe.' (2) Considering adding e-bike repair services but hasn't decided if it's worth buying the diagnostic tools (~$800) given how few e-bike customers ask — genuinely on the fence.
